claim_location: parquet schema metadata of the day's one object
words: Each built day of the Cottonwood filled report carries, in the parquet schema metadata of its one object, the date of the newest account_dim partition as households_as_of and the word held as households_claim: the current household membership applied to a past day, not measured as of that day. Each built day also counts, and never silently drops, two sets: the distinct accounts of its own returns partition that no household holds (accounts_dropped), and the households with no account row on the day (households_no_rows). The four values are stated in the handler result, on a dry run too, and the two counts are printed on the built-day line. Account and household ids never leave the handler: they are not printed, returned or written to any metadata, and only counts and dates reach the output. Not proven: the Lambda runtime, the first real build against the Cottonwood bucket, and how any page prints the claim, which is a reader's change and is not made here.
